chunks: From him, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Bukayr ibn A'yan, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, when he banished someone from the people of Islam, would banish him to the nearest town of the people of shirk to Islam. So he considered that, and al-Daylam was the nearest of the people of shirk to Islam.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: title of Imam 'Ali عليه السلام, the Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.أَهْلِ الشِّرْكِ: the people of shirk, non-Muslims described here in legal-geographical context
key_terms.أَهْلِ الْإِسْلَامِ: the people belonging to the Muslim community
key_terms.الدَّيْلَمُ: al-Daylam, identified here as the nearest such region
key_terms.بَلْدَةٍ: a town or locality to which the exile was directed
key_terms.نَفَى: to banish or exile as a punitive measure

ai.seo_question: Where did Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام send a Muslim when imposing banishment?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a judicial practice of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام regarding the banishment of a Muslim. It states that exile was carried out to the nearest land of the people of shirk adjacent to the Muslim realm, and in this case al-Daylam was regarded as the nearest such region.
